text.content:
Split a site's security into components and give each a level from 0 (none) to 4 (the best available). Level 4 components tend to be active measures; levels 3 and below tend to be passive. Each level includes what the lower levels have. Equipment found at a level has a rating equal to that level; if a device first appears at a lower level than the one you chose, a rating of twice the chosen level is a good rule of thumb (CSH p.94–96).

AreaComponentsWhat the levels add (summary)
Physicalbarriers, lighting, guards, security animals1 reinforced interior doors, perimeter lights, guards at entrances · 2 fences, spotlights, scheduled patrols with mundane animals · 3 slab-to-slab walls, lighting everywhere, officers at all entrances and random patrols · 4 living walls against astral intrusion, IR/low-level/magical lighting, constant patrols with paranormal or cybered animals
Technicalalarms and access control; surveillance1 Type 1–2 maglocks, exterior CCTV · 2 door/window sensors, fence alarms, Type 2–3 maglocks, interior CCTV, an on-call rigger · 3 volumetric and door sensors, Type 3 maglocks (biometric in sensitive areas), patrol drones, a full-time rigger on CCSS · 4 Type 4 and biometric maglocks, interior drone patrols, extensive CCSS and fixed drone emplacements
Magicalon-site magical security1 a corporate magician on call · 2 a full-time security magician · 3 wards and/or a fiber-optic observation network · 4 watchers, nature spirits or elementals patrolling, alarms and fast-response teams
Matrixthe site's private matrix1 corporate deckers on call · 2 full-time deckers on site, in the matrix during external alerts · 3 in the matrix during internal alerts · 4 a security decker in the matrix around the clock
Personnelscreening of employees1 background computer checks and a few interviews · 2 full investigations back fifteen years · 3 active security-awareness programs · 4 periodic loyalty checks, re-investigations and lie-detector tests

Add up the levels of all the components and divide by 6, rounding down. Well-trained, motivated staff can push it up (to a maximum of 4 for a Level 3 system); overworked or poorly trained staff can pull it down. The OSL never goes above 5 or below 0. For a megacorp rated in Corporate Shadowfiles, halve its Security Rating, rounding down (CSH p.98).

Defeating a component with dice: the appropriate skill test against a target number of twice the component's level, needing successes equal to the OSL. Failure sets off an alarm, and the test is needed every time the component is passed — on the way out too (CSH p.104). Roleplaying around a system (finding its designer, a disgruntled employee) is often easier, especially for fat bacteria.

Impact armor gives half (round down) protection against wire, and Combat Pool can't be used to resist it. Damage goes to the wire itself; clippers double the cutter's Strength, and each 2 successes on a Strength Test against the Barrier add 1 (CSH p.99). Spotting modifiers: brush +1 to +4, distracted or running +2, fluctuating light +1 for the worst level.

Pressure sensorPerception TNSensitivity: normal / animals / drones
Pressure mesh87 / 4 / 3

A pressure sensor can be noticed with a Perception Test; failing a second one at −2 means it was stepped on, and a Reaction Test against the sensitivity plus natural Body takes the weight off before it triggers (+2 if running). Motion sensors are beaten by moving very slowly (half a metre per turn) with a Stealth Test against their rating; an ultrasound emitter/detector (Concealability 8, (Rating × 2)/72 hrs, Rating × 400¥, SI 3) contests them. Vibration detectors are 6 to 10+; trip beams are bypassed with a Quickness Test of 4–8, or 8/12/16 for proxy emitters by how much of the design you know (CSH p.99–100).

Keypads and cardreaders come in two steps (CSH p.100–101, from the Neo-Anarchists' Guide):

  1. Remove the casing: Electronics (B/R) Test against the casing's Barrier Rating (usually the keypad's rating), base 60 seconds; any anti-tamper alarm rating adds to the TN, and failing it triggers the alarm.
  2. Tamper with the circuits: Electronics Test against the keypad's rating, base 60 seconds; failure trips a passive alert. A cardreader's casing is twice its rating and tampering is at +2.

Sequencers (Rating 1–6, 500¥ × Rating²) still need the casing off: roll the sequencer's rating against the keypad's rating while the keypad rolls its rating against the sequencer's; base 10 seconds; if the keypad gets more successes, a passive alert. A passcard works the same way without removing the casing (10 seconds; failure triggers an alarm); a maglock passcard costs 10,000¥ × Rating².

Print scanners (Rating 1–10): phony prints are Rating 1–8 at 200¥ per point and need an Intelligence (3) Test to cast; a severed finger or hand is Rating 8 and loses a point an hour (one per 3 hours with care). Retinal duplication is 50,000¥ + 25,000¥ per extra point; Essence .1 at Rating 1, .25 at 2–4, .5 at 5+. To beat a scanner, it rolls its rating against the fake's rating; one success detects the fake. Tampering with a scanner is as a keypad at +4.

To take over a rigged system an outside rigger needs a hardwire access point, a dataline tap (rating + Electronics against twice the surveillance level, successes equal to the OSL), to defeat any encryption (decryption module rating + Intelligence against twice the alarm/access level) and to adjust to the protocols (emulation module rating + Intelligence against twice the surveillance level) — each needing successes equal to the OSL, or the system goes on alert (CSH p.104–105).

Then the two riggers fight: rigged Initiative; the attacker makes an opposed Willpower Test (Control Pool may add dice, to a maximum of Willpower); greater net successes deal (Willpower)L Stun, +1 level per 2 successes, resisted with Body (Control Pool to a maximum of Body). Attacking is a Complex Action; disengaging (jacking out) is Free. A decker can fight a rigged system with a System Control Rig Emulator: no programs, +2 to all tests, Initiative −2 with no Response Increase dice, Control Pool half the emulation utility's rating (round up), and damage as from black IC (SR2 p.171).
